newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sees oil/gas earning $12.5 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sees oil/gas earning $12.5 bln in 1997.

text.p: Algeria forecast that oil and gas exports would earn it $12.5 billion this year, up by $1.0 billion on its initial forecasts.
The Algerian news agency, outlining the main points of the budget to be debated by parliament this week, said on Tuesday:

"Concerning new elements that have arisen since the Finance Law for 1997 was drawn up, hydrocarbon export income will be around $12.5 billion at the end of the year instead of the $11.5 billion originally envisaged."
Last year, OPEC-member Algeria earned $12.6 billion from hydrocarbon sales abroad -- the source of more than 90 percent of the country's hard currency.
APS said the new forecast followed a 13.1 percent rise in the price, and 7.9 percent in volume, of its hydrocarbon exports in the first five months of this year compared to the same period in 1996.
Algeria's oil quota under the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is set at 750,000 barrels per day.

The North African country exports about 30 billion cubic metres of gas a year in addition to crude liftings. In its three year plan now being debated by parliament the value of annual hydrocarbon exports is forecast to reach $15 billion .
The latest Reuters survey showed Algeria's wellhead output in July stood at 860,000 barrels per day, after running at 850,000 bpd for the earlier part of the year.
